title: Round Robin CPU Scheduling
purpose: Preemptive time-sliced CPU scheduling providing fair execution time for all active processes in the Ready Queue.
spatialLayout: Horizontal flow: processes enter Ready Queue on left, execute in central CPU core, and preempt back to tail via upper feedback loop.
keyPoints: Fair time-sharing algorithm with zero starvation.
Controlled by a fixed time quantum parameter.
Gantt chart displays chronological execution slices.
If quantum is too large, degrades to First-Come First-Served.

title: Binary Search Flowchart
purpose: Search sorted array in logarithmic O(log n) time by halving search space at each decision.
keyPoints: Prerequisite: Array must be sorted in ascending order.
Calculates midpoint pivot index mid = (low + high) / 2.
Discards half of search space after each comparison.
Terminates when low > high (target absent) or arr[mid] == target.
ocrText: Start -> low=0, high=n-1 -> Decision: low <= high? -> Yes: mid=(low+high)/2 -> Decision: arr[mid] == target? -> Yes: Found! Return mid. -> No: arr[mid] > target? -> Yes: high=mid-1, No: low=mid+1. Decision: low <= high? No: Return -1. End.
audioScript: This content is a Flowchart: Binary Search Flowchart. This flowchart diagrams Binary Search Divide-and-Conquer Algorithm. The flowchart starts with a rounded oval marked Start. An arrow points downward to a rectangle setting low to 0 and high to n minus 1. Next, a diamond represents the loop condition: Is low less than or equal to high? The No path leads directly to a terminal oval: Target Not Found, returning negative 1. The Yes path leads to a rectangular process calculating mid as low plus high divided by 2. A second diamond checks: Does target equal arr at mid? The Yes path reaches an exit oval announcing: Found Target at mid, returning mid. The No path leads to a third decision diamond: Is target less than arr at mid? The Yes path sets high equal to mid minus 1 to inspect the left sub-array. The No path sets low equal to mid plus 1 to inspect the right sub-array. Both branches loop back to the initial condition diamond until the item is found or space is exhausted.

title: Quadratic Formula and Root Equation
purpose: Finds real and complex roots of any second-degree polynomial equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0.
spokenMath: x equals negative b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4 a c, all divided by 2 a.
keyPoints: x equals negative b plus or minus square root of b squared minus 4ac over 2a.
Discriminant determines root nature: positive (2 real), zero (1 real), negative (2 complex conjugate).
Coefficient a must be non-zero.
ocrText: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a). For ax² + bx + c = 0. Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac.
audioScript: This content is a Formula: Quadratic Formula and Root Equation. The formula is: x equals negative b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4 a c, all divided by 2 a. Significance: Solves any quadratic polynomial of the form a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero. Here is what each symbol means: x, Roots of equation: The unknown variable values where the parabola intersects the x-axis. a, Quadratic coefficient: Coefficient of x squared; governs vertical stretching and whether parabola opens upward or downward. b, Linear coefficient: Coefficient of x; influences axis of symmetry. c, Constant term: The y-intercept of the quadratic function. Plus or Minus sign: Indicates two distinct solution branches for the two potential roots. Discriminant b squared minus 4ac: If greater than 0, two real roots. If equal to 0, one repeated root. If negative, two complex conjugate roots. Example application: For 2 x squared minus 4 x minus 6 equals 0, roots are x equals 3 and x equals negative 1.

title: Python Bubble Sort Algorithm
purpose: Sorts an array in ascending order by repeatedly swapping adjacent inverted elements.
keyPoints: Implemented in Python
Nested loops with quadratic O(n^2) worst-case time complexity.
Optimizable to O(n) best case with a swapped boolean flag.
audioScript: This content is a Code: Python Bubble Sort Algorithm. The code is written in Python. Its purpose is to sorts a list of elements in ascending order by repeatedly swapping adjacent elements that are out of order. Overall logic: The algorithm iterates over the array multiple times. In each pass, the largest unsorted element bubbles up to its correct final position at the end of the list. Here is the line by line breakdown: Line 1 defines the function bubble_sort accepting an input array arr. Line 2 calculates the length of the array n = len(arr). Line 3 initiates an outer loop iterating index i from 0 to n minus 1, tracking the number of sorted passes. Line 4 starts an inner loop index j from 0 to n minus i minus 1 to compare adjacent pairs. Line 5 evaluates the conditional check: if arr[j] is strictly greater than arr[j plus 1]. Line 6 executes a simultaneous swap exchanging arr[j] with arr[j plus 1]. Line 7 returns the sorted array. Potential concern: Quadratic Time Complexity Bottleneck. Correction: Add a boolean flag swapped that halts the algorithm early in O(n) time if no elements were swapped during a pass. For input Unsorted array, the output produced is Ascending sorted array.
